Commentary.Commentary: The surface is a real beauty for batting. Bangladesh will back themselves to get a big lead here but for that to happen they will have to bat well. Stay with us as their openers will be out soon to begin the home side's reply.

Anyway, Zimbabwe won't be too disappointed with their first innings total. It's true that they would have aimed something above 300 but Bangladesh bowled a lot better this morning to not let them achieve that target. Apart from Peter Moor, we saw Hamilton Masakadza and Sean Williams also playing vital knocks on Day 1. The rest of the batting unit didn't turn up much though. For Bangladesh, they sweat hard yesterday to get five wickets while today was a relatively easier task. Taijul Islam was the standout bowler with a 6-fer and he was supported nicely by his spin partners.

Right then, Zimbabwe didn't concede many runs this morning to pick the remaining five wickets. They gave away just 46 runs but it took them 26.3 overs to do that. Peter Moor and Regis Chakabva started watchfully and raised their 50-run stand but soon after that, the latter departed. Moor, however, continued to bat watchfully and didn't try to farm the strike. He could have adopted a different approach and it was a bit strange to watch him let go the strike so easily.

He goes at it with firm hands and gets an outside edge. Liton Das at silly point shows great reflexes as he pouches the ball in no time. Mehidy Hasan gives an interview to Shamim Chowdhury. He says that they were looking for wickets on Day 1 but feels the pitch was very good for batting. Adds that they were not getting much help and their strategy was to keep it tidy. States that the surface today will be better and he hopes to get some turn.

Zimbabwe's head coach, Lalchand Rajput says that they have started this Test well and feels they should have lost one wicket less. He is still hopeful of getting a total around 300 runs. Informs that they had camps in Harare to practice playing spin and they are well prepared. Wishes that the second day also goes well for his team. Wants his boys to execute the plans well and signs off by saying that the first hour will be very crucial.

Pitch report - Ed Rainsford points out the marks on the pitch and tells it's very dry. He feels that the abrasive nature of the surface will assist the pacers too and it could be conducive for reverse swing.

Welcome ladies and gentlemen for the second day of the first Test match at this brand new venue for the longer format in Sylhet. We witnessed some excellent cricket on Day 1 where against the common notion, Zimbabwe batted bravely against the spinners and have got a good total on the board. Hamilton Masakadza, Sean Williams and then Peter Moor showed resolve and character in their approach and the latter is still unbeaten. The African team will wish that he continues and takes their total to somewhere near 350, if not more. The Bangla bowlers didn't get the kind of success which was expected from them but still by picking 5 wickets, they have done a decent job. It will be all about finishing the Zimbabwean innings as soon as possible. Let's see what happens today.
... DAY 2, 1ST SESSION ...

All the Bangladesh bowlers were decent but their persistence did not win them big dividends. While it is true that they are only a wicket away from getting into the tail, what is equally true is that if the visitors manage to add another 30-40 runs on Day 2 without losing a wicket, they will be in a good position to cross 300 and get to 325-350 which will then become a very good score on this track. Join us on Sunday, November 4, 2018 at 1000 local (0400 GMT) for all the action from Day 2. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

A bit of a strange innings from Peter Moor though. One can understand that he wanted to take his time on a tricky pitch but it was by no means, one where you could score only at a strike rate of 30. He might want to increase that scoring rate come Sunday and steer his side past 300.

Sean Williams and Hamilton Masakadza were the heroes for their side. The captain took control with two early wickets down while the latter ensured that there was no collapse with decent partnerships in the middle order. He missed out on a century but that was more due to the superb catching by Mehidy Hasan.

Not quite sure who would be happy or unhappy at the moment. Zimbabwe would feel that they have won a good toss on a pitch which will degrade with each passing day, but then Bangladesh have not allowed them to run away with the game. They have been tight and disciplined and kept the run flow under check. A wicket quickly in the morning and they can still restrict the visitors under 260.

Yawn... it has been that sort of a session. 87 runs were scored, in 29 overs, for the loss of a wicket but the last hour was nothing less than attritional. When Williams fell, Zimbabwe were just beginning to accelerate - after he went, only 35 runs came in 87 balls.

We are back for the final session of the day. We hope we get some good cricketing action unlike the snooze-fest in the previous. Bangladesh will look to get a wicket or two and then run through the tail. The visitors should try and score a bit quicker. Abu Jayed will bowl the first over post Tea.
... Day 1, Session 3 ...

Zimbabwe, on the other hand, have gone into a non-scoring mode. At one point of time, there were 6 maidens on the trot. Not quite sure whether they will be going anywhere by just blocking. Just 28 overs left in the day, so we definitely won't be going into overtime. Join us back at 3 pm local (0900 GMT).
An attritional session. Just 64 runs scored in 31 overs for the loss of Hamilton Masakadza. The pitch is still turning but the Bangladeshi bowlers could not quite extract much.

OUT! That has gone through and the Cobra dance has begun! Nazmul gets the fourth wicket for Bangladesh. Nothing really special about that delivery, just plain lack of technique from the batsman. He has simply failed to read a straight ball. He comes half-forward to defend, probably in two minds, thinking whether this will turn away or go straight on. He is not to the pitch of the ball and as a result, misses it. The cherry goes past the inside edge, hits the back pad and then the timber. The bat came down very late, because Raza probably was thinking to play it from the crease initially. The 44-run stand has been disturbed. So the third partnership which has got a start but not carried on.

Bangladesh have been clinical so far. They have not done anything extraordinary, only stuck to basics and allowed the pitch to do the rest. However, partnerships might frustrate them. They will know that anything close to 300 on this surface will be tricky. Join us back at 1240 local (0640 GMT) for the second session.

Finally a milestone to celebrate for the skipper. He has struggled to get past the 20s but so far, he has looked a mixture of composed and rash. He started strongly but then got a little bit careless in the middle. Escaped a few nervous moments but has managed to survive. Williams has looked good in his short stay thus far.

A shared opening session. Bangladesh threatened to run through the batting with truckloads of spin but Zimbabwe have done just enough to make sure that they have not lost more than 2 wickets. Chari's dismissal was a wild slog while Taylor's one was an excellent catch. But the seeds of those wickets were sown through some tight and disciplined bowling.

OUT! The catch is legal! What a take from Nazmul Hossain Shanto. Excellent reflexes. Full and around middle, the arm ball, Taylor looked to defend but the ball darted in and flew off the inside edge. It went straight to short leg but he barely had time to react. Shanto caught it and then started to celebrate but only Rahim and he were celebrating. Taijul was amused. The umpire was not sure at all and referred it upstairs, after conferring with his partner. The soft signal was out and replays show why. The ball was actually dipping down onto Shanto but he managed to pick it up with his left hand! Superb stuff.

Chari wants the single and is halfway down the track. Hamilton realizes late and then sets off. The fielder comes charging in, has a shy at the striker's end but misses. Chari was a goner, had that hit.
On middle and leg, Chari prods forward and gets it through fine leg for a single.
Full and down the leg side, Chari looks to flick but misses.
Change of ends for Taijul.
Another good length delivery swinging away from the batsman, Hamilton  leaves it alone.
Length delivery on off stump, Hamilton defends of the front foot.
Good length delivery on middle stump, Hamilton flicks it towards mid on.
Good length delivery outside off stump, Hamilton looks to cut but checks it at the last moment.
Landed outside off, Masakadza pushes it towards point.
Full and outside off, watchfully pushed towards mid off.
Ariful Haque introduced. Bangladesh under early pressure.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball. Easy catch for the keeper behind the stumps. A strong appeal from the bowler and fielders. The umpire shows no interest in the appeal.
FOUR! Short outside off stump, Hamilton cuts it towards point for a beautiful boundary.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Bowls down the leg side, Chari looks to flick but misses.
FOUR! Driven through mid on by the batsman. The ball races to the boundary. The umpire signals a boundary.
Good length delivery on middle stump, Chari defends of the front foot.
SIX! Up and over! Full and outside off, Masakadza comes forward and lofts it over long off!
Gets right forward to this one and blocks.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
FOUR! Nicely done. Full and around leg stump, Hamilton gets down and sweeps it behind square leg for a boundary!
Full on middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Good length delivery on off stump, Chari tucks it towards third man and gets a couple.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.
Driven towards the mid on region.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Good length delivery outside off stump, Chari left it alone.
Bowls a yorker on off stump, Hamilton brings his bat down in time and gets a single towards the point region.
Full and outside off, pushed towards point again.
Landed outside off, turning away, shouldered arms to.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and outside off, pushed wide of silly point, a bit aerially.
Landed outside off, pushed towards point.
Quicker one, the arm ball. Chari gets a good stride forward and defends.
Comes forward and keeps it out.
Stays back in his crease and blocks.
The batsman fails to get bat on that one and is hit on the pad. They pick up a single. Leg bye given by the umpire.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Well outside off, left alone.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
SIX! Ho ho ho! Handsome hit! Full and outside off, Masakadza just lofts it through the line and clears long off!
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on again.
Around off, defended towards mid on.
Very wide delivery, miles outside off, Brian is not chasing that.

NOT OUT. INSIDE EDGE! Bangladesh have lost a review in the third over of the innings. A lovely nut, pitching outside off on a length and coming back in sharply, Chari looked to defend but then there was a slight away movement. As a result, he got squared up and was hit on the pads. Jayed appealed but the umpire turned it down. On taking the review, it was found that Snickometer detected an outside edge!
Huge LBW shout! Not given. The bowler seems to be confident and Mahmudullah has gone for the review. Looks close...
Full and outside off, driven through point cover for a couple. Gets off the mark in fine style.
Landed outside off, a touch wide too, left alone.
Full and miles outside off, let through once again.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Just outside off, solidly blocked towards point. Tidy start by Taijul.
Full and outside off, spinning away, left alone.

HUGE APPEAL FOR A CAUGHT BEHIND! NEARLY PLAYED ON TOO! Landed around middle, Hamilton goes back to flick but gets a thick inside edge. The ball then deflects onto the pads, bounces onto the ground and goes past leg stump into Rahim's gloves! Mushhfiqur thinks that the ball has hit the boot, hence appeals for the catch but then is informed by the bowler that it bounced.
Fuller in length, solidly defended to the off side.
A tad short, Masakadza goes to pull but the ball bounces steeply after pitching and the captain is taken aback. Fends it to the off side.
Full and outside off, driven straight to short extra cover.
Taijul Islam to bowl from the other end. So we shall be having spin from the first over at this end.
Landed outside off, shouldered arms to.

Excellent shot, terrific fielding. But, has Mahmudullah hurt himself? Full and outside off, Hamilton drives it through the covers. The ball almost makes it to the ropes but skipper Mahmudullah hares after it and then dives near the ropes to haul the ball back in. Then, he clutches his hamstring in pain. Ouch. Three runs taken.
This one comes back in,  Hamilton feels for it but is beaten.
Full and just outside off, left alone.
Similar ball, probably even wider than the previous one, Masakadza shoulders arms again.
Good start. On a length outside off, swinging away, but a bit too wide to be played at. Left alone.

The players now make their way out to the middle. Brian Chari and Hamilton Masakadza are the openers for Zimbabwe. Abu Jayed, the lone seamer for the home side, will start off proceedings. Here we go!

Mahmudullah agrees that he would have batted first too, given the dryness of the wicket but now looks forward to restricting Zimbabwe to a small total. On the absence of Tamim and Shakib, the skipper looks at it as a great opportunity for youngsters to step up in the seniors' absence. Admits that in the past, Bangladesh have not done too well but here is a chance to rectify those mistakes. Informs that Ariful Haque and Nazmul Islam are making their Test debut and the composition consists of 3 spinners.

Hamilton is all smiles. States that it is very warm out there and also, he expects the pitch to turn from today itself, so the decision. Admits that the team could not get the ideal preparation in the warm-up but no one can do anything about it. Adds that the team would like to take every opportunity that comes by. Informs that Zimbabwe are going in with 2 seamers and 2 spinners, with Brandon Mavuta and Wellington Masakadza debuting today.
TOSS - Time for the spin of the coin. Mahmudullah flips it, Masakadaza calls Heads and it is a Head. ZIMBABWE CHOOSE TO BAT FIRST.

PITCH REPORT - Ed Rainsford doing the pitch report observes that there are already cracks visible on Day 1 itself - which means, the track looks very very dry, Also, he informs that the pitch was covered the whole of yesterday under the Hessian, so there will be some moisture too. No doubt - there will be plenty of turn.
Weather Report - It is bright and sunny for now and hopefully it stays that way.

Hello and warm welcome to the first Test between Bangladesh and Zimbabwe. The hosts had won the ODI series convincingly, but the African nation would be looking for   some respite in the Test series and improve their performance. The match is happening at Sylhet International Stadium, becoming the 8th venue in Bangladesh hosting a Test.  Brendan Taylor and Sean Williams are the experienced players for Zimbabwe, but they could not do much in the ODIs. Bangladesh will be missing the likes of Tamim and Shakib.   Their strength is spin, so spinners should come into play. It is time that skipper Hamilton Masakadza performs according to the expectations set by the Zimbabwe team. A bit of   rain is forecast but hopefully there will be no major delay during the course of the match.
